title: Adani Green Shares Fall 4% After Q2 Results as Brokers Split on Grid Bottlenecks
excerpt: Profit rose 15% to Rs 673 crore and power-supply EBITDA jumped 51%, but weak grid availability knocked the stock; Jefferies kept a Buy at Rs 1,695 while JM Financial held Add at Rs 1,374.
body:
• Adani Green Energy's Q2 FY27 consolidated net profit rose 15% year on year to Rs 673 crore, with total income up 39% to Rs 4,520 crore.
  • Power-supply revenue grew 45% to Rs 4,019 crore and its EBITDA surged 51% to Rs 3,835 crore, at a 92% margin.
  • Shares still fell 4% intraday to Rs 1,211 on Thursday as investors focused on grid availability — solar availability dropped to 78.9% in H1 amid transmission delays.
  • Jefferies retained Buy with a Rs 1,695 target; JM Financial retained Add at Rs 1,374, calling results largely in line with expectations.

Shares of Adani Green Energy fell 4% to Rs 1,211 on the BSE on Thursday after the company reported second-quarter results that paired strong operating growth with a visible bottleneck: the grid could not take all the power its plants were ready to supply, The Economic Times reported.

Consolidated net profit rose 15% year on year to Rs 673 crore, from Rs 583 crore a year earlier, while total income increased 39% to Rs 4,520 crore. The core power-supply business did the heavy lifting: revenue up 45% to Rs 4,019 crore and EBITDA up 51% to Rs 3,835 crore, with the segment margin improving to 92% from 90.5%. Operational capacity grew 24% to 20.8 GW, keeping the company on its path toward a 50 GW target by 2030, and energy sales rose 33% in the quarter.

The bottleneck: plants ready, wires late

The drag is transmission. JM Financial noted that grid availability weakened amid delays in transmission lines: solar, wind and hybrid grid availability stood at 78.9%, 93.7% and 94.5% respectively in the first half, against 89%, 97.4% and 89% a year earlier — even though the plants themselves maintained availability above 99%. Generation assets are being commissioned faster than the evacuation infrastructure around mega-sites such as Khavda, where operational capacity has reached 10.8 GW of a planned 30 GW.

The company's partial answer is storage. Installed battery storage reached 6.6 GWh, with a target above 10 GWh by the end of FY27, letting it shift power to hours when the grid can take it. First-half capital expenditure was about Rs 16,000 crore alongside debt drawdowns of Rs 13,700 crore, according to JM Financial's reading of the results.

What the brokers say

Jefferies retained its Buy rating with a target price of Rs 1,695, citing reasonable valuations after a 22% correction from the stock's peak. The brokerage values the company at about 20 times one-year forward EV/EBITDA and projects a 30% EBITDA compound annual growth rate between FY26 and FY30, helped by rising power demand, improving utilisation at Khavda and the expanding storage business. It also flagged a demand tailwind: possible El Niño conditions into 2027 could bring higher temperatures and power shortages, with coal stocks already at critical levels of under seven days.

JM Financial retained its Add rating with a Rs 1,374 target, describing results as largely in line with expectations and noting the power-supply EBITDA margin of about 91% beat its 89% estimate. The split in targets — Rs 1,695 against Rs 1,374 — is effectively a split on how quickly India's transmission build-out catches up with its renewable generation. That, more than quarterly profit, is what the stock now trades on.
